summary: Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje worked in religious studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1874–1880), the Nederlands-Indische Bestuursacademie, and under Theodor Nöldeke (~1880–1881). He held positions at Leiden University (1887, 1889–1890, 1906–1927) and the Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland (~1920–1921).

Christian August Brandis was a philosopher and historian who studied at Kiel University (~1808–1812). He held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1816), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1816–1821), and the University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae studied Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics at Munich, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1872–1878) under teachers including Ernst Curtius, Friedrich Spiegel, and Heinrich Hübschmann. He held professorships at Halle, Münster, Giessen, Strasbourg, and Heidelberg (1909–1924).

Christian Bernert works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna (Mag. phil.) under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen worked in linguistics, religious studies, and archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen (under Christian Gottlob Heyne), Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Prussian envoy (~1823–1854).

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University (PhD ~1999–2003) under Jay L. Garfield and John Powers. He later served at the College of Charleston (~2006).

Christian Ferstl works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he held a lectorate in 2014, and worked as a research project collaborator at the University of Leipzig in 2021.
Christian Gilberti works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2026), where he also held a post in South and Southeast Asian Studies.

Christian Gottlob Heyne specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He earned his master's degree at the University of Leipzig (1748–1752). He was appointed professor at the University of Göttingen (1763) and director of the Göttingen State and University Library (1764–1812).

Christian Haskett specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Witzel, and held a post at Centre College (attested 2018–2019).

Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman. He taught at the University of Copenhagen (2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Bonn (Ph.D. 1821–1827) under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He spent his career at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and full professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard University, and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~1996–2003). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and the University of Washington (from 2007).
Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served as a professor there (attested 1980–1995).

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Magister and Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. His career includes serving as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art and senior lecturer at SOAS University of London (2014).
Christian Mabel Duff was a scholar in the field of Indology. She completed her studies at Kiel University, where she was taught by Paul Deussen.

Christian Matthias Boehm studied biochemistry at TU Munich, systems biology at Imperial College London, scientific computing at Cambridge, and completed a PhD at SOAS under Toshifumi Konno. He later held posts at the Max Planck Institute (2017–2018) and BMBF (2019).

Christian Schweigaard Stang was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1918–1927) under Sten Konow and Antoine Meillet, and subsequently served at Oslo as associate professor (1930) and professor of Slavic philology (1938–1970).

Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and held posts at the Chunghwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (1998–2001) and Kyoto University, where he served as professor (attested 1993, 2012).

Christian von Ehrenfels was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna (~1878–1886) and the University of Graz (~1886–1887). He held a post at the University of Vienna (~1888–1896) before serving as professor of philosophy at the German University in Prague (~1896–1929).
